practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior with a single Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make root causes clear. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if only ONE Act operation; non-compliant if multiple distinct method calls/acts exist. DECISION RULES: 1) Count Act operations. 2) If >1, non-compliant. In this test the code calls pilha0.empilha(...) and then calls desempilha (via invokeDesempilha) — two distinct Act operations (push and pop) in the same test method. VERDICT: non-compliant because there are multiple Act operations testing more than one step/behavior in the same test.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not depend on other tests or shared mutable state. RATIONALE: Independence allows arbitrary execution order. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if uses local variables only or uses setup/teardown. DECISION RULES: 1) Check for @Before/@After. 2) If only local variables used, compliant. This test constructs a Pilha locally and uses no shared static/instance state; there are no setup/teardown annotations required. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should include happy paths and error/exception scenarios. RATIONALE: Verifies robustness and error handling. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if there are at least two tests covering success and error (or assertThrows/@Test(expected=...)). DECISION RULES: 1) Look for exception tests. 2) If class has only happy-path tests, non-compliant. This class has a single test exercising a normal push/pop scenario and contains no assertion or handling for exceptional cases (no assertThrows, no @Test(expected=...), no tests for invalid inputs). VERDICT: non-compliant because no exceptional/error case is tested.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should include boundary values like empty strings, zero, negatives. RATIONALE: Boundaries commonly reveal off-by-one errors. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if test data includes empty string/zero/min/max. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for empty string/0/-1 etc. This test explicitly uses an empty string for the pushed value (pushed = "") and checks sizes 0 and 1, which exercises a relevant boundary. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and avoid duplication; repeated setup should be factored out. RATIONALE: Modularity reduces duplication and eases maintenance. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if helper methods/constants used or if no duplication exists. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for helper methods/constants. 2) If only a single short test without repetition, acceptable. This class contains one test only and no repeated setup across methods; no duplication is observable in the provided snippet. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and low complexity. RATIONALE: Simpler tests are easier to understand and less buggy. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if methods are short (<20-30 lines) and have no loops/complex conditionals. DECISION RULES: 1) If >30 lines or contains loops/complex conditionals, non-compliant. This test is linear, contains only a single simple if (popped != null) and no loops; it is not overly long or complex. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should be comprehensive to detect faults. RATIONALE: Deeper assertions reveal subtle bugs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if multiple properties are verified (>=2 assertions on result). DECISION RULES: 1) If only one superficial assertion, non-compliant. This test performs multiple meaningful assertions: instance creation, size before/after, type check of popped value, equality check when non-null. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or disabled tests; keep suite active. RATIONALE: Ignored tests may hide regressions. EVALUATION CRITERIA: non-compliant if @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test present. DECISION RULES: 1) Search for @Ignore/@Disabled. None present. The test is active and runnable. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should link to requirement IDs or stories. RATIONALE: Traceability aids impact analysis. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if annotations or Javadoc reference requirement IDs. DECISION RULES: 1) Search for @Story/@Requirement or REQ-/JIRA- in comments. Neither annotations nor requirement identifiers are present in the method/class. VERDICT: non-compliant because there is no traceability information linking this test to a requirement or ticket.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests should be explicit and separate. RATIONALE: Non-functional requirements must be validated. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant only if explicit performance/security tests are present. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for @Test(timeout=...) or explicit security checks. This test method declares @Test(timeout = 4000) which is an explicit performance/time assertion in JUnit 4. VERDICT: compliant because a timeout is present.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should describe scenario and expected outcome. RATIONALE: Good names make tests self-documenting. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if name follows methodName_scenario_expectedBehavior. DECISION RULES: 1) Check if name follows pattern. The method name is test1 (generic) despite in-body Given-When-Then comments; the name does not describe scenario/expected result. VERDICT: non-compliant due to non-descriptive test method name.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Generated tests should be minimal and intention-revealing. RATIONALE: Heavy generated tests are verbose and hard to maintain. EVALUATION CRITERIA: non-compliant if there are signs of code generation (auto-generated comments, repetitive names). DECISION RULES: 1) Look for auto-generated comments or repetitive test names. The class imports EvoSuite runtime artifacts and retains the autogenerated-style name test1 (and header comment mentions keeping original method names), which are indicative of generated tests and repetitive naming. VERDICT: non-compliant due to clear signs of test generation and non-descriptive naming.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show design intent (Given-When-Then or BDD naming). RATIONALE: Test-first design and clear structure improve coverage. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if Given-When-Then comments or BDD-style naming present. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for Given-When-Then. This method includes Given-When-Then comments at the top of the test body indicating an intent-driven structure. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should test public behavior and avoid coupling to implementation details (reflection). RATIONALE: Reflection or checking internals makes tests brittle. EVALUATION CRITERIA: non-compliant if reflection APIs are used. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for reflection usage (getDeclaredField, Method, InvocationTargetException). This file imports java.lang.reflect.Method and InvocationTargetException and the test invokes desempilha via invokeDesempilha (reflection helper), indicating reflection is used to access behavior instead of calling the public API directly. VERDICT: non-compliant because reflection usage is present making tests coupled to implementation details.
practices_evaluation.improved_code:
Object popped = pilha0.desempilha();
org.junit.Assert.assertTrue("Popped value should be String or null", popped == null || popped instanceof String);

practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use clear, specific assertions with messages. RATIONALE: Descriptive assertions make failures easier to diagnose. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if assertions have messages and use specific assertion methods. DECISION RULES: 1) Check for assertions with messages. This test uses assertNotNull/assertEquals/assertTrue with descriptive messages and multiple specific assertions. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain the 'why' and be minimal. RATIONALE: Helpful comments aid maintenance; excessive comments clutter. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if comments are minimal and explain intent. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for commented-out code. 2) If comments describe Given-When-Then intent, compliant. The test contains Given-When-Then comments that document intent and no commented-out code. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must be deterministic (no random/time effects). RATIONALE: Deterministic tests avoid flakiness. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if no Random/System.currentTimeMillis/Thread.sleep usage. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for random/time/sleep usage. The test uses no random values, no time-based calls, and no sleeps; state is local to the test. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should not leave side effects or persistent state. RATIONALE: Side effects cause inter-test interference. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if tests clean up or avoid persistent side effects. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for persistent changes without cleanup. This test manipulates only an in-memory Pilha instance and does not create files, modify static state, or leave resources open. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use labels/categories to organize tests for selective execution. RATIONALE: Categorization helps CI filtering. EVALUATION CRITERIA: compliant if @Tag/@Category annotations present. DECISION RULES: 1) Look for @Tag/@Category. The class/method contains no labeling annotations. VERDICT: non-compliant because no test category/label is applied.
